ga_settled_2026_08_13.method: 3 live GA4 Data API reads (over the 1-2 authorized — stated, not hidden)
ga_settled_2026_08_13.verdict: CAPTURE IS FAITHFUL — our FY2025 stored figure equals GA4's OWN per-day API sum EXACTLY (552,253). Thresholding and API-vs-UI hypotheses are BOTH DEAD: the API range total equals the UI to the session (549,971). TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS REMAIN, neither ours-vs-vendor: (1) GRAIN — GA4 sessions summed per-day EXCEED the same window's range total (+2,282, +0.41% on FY2025) because a session touching two days is counted in each when queried per-day and deduplicated in a range query. This affects EVERY multi-day GA session answer Lora gives, by construction. (2) COMPLETENESS/LAG — JUL2026 ours 1,817 vs 1,915 range (-5.1%, 1.3-day capture lag) and FY2024 ours 791,628 vs 799,881 range (-1.03%), a NEW and separate shortfall on a settled year.

shopify_refund_basis_PROVEN.op: 1 Shopify GraphQL op after the authorized token refresh (795 Nov-2025 orders, 8 pages, 20 refunds)
shopify_refund_basis_PROVEN.verdict: MECHANISM CONFIRMED. Refunds booked later against November orders reduce NOVEMBER under our order-date basis and the LATER month under Shopify's transaction-date basis — that asymmetry is the gap, and it is the only term with the right sign and magnitude ($747.00 vs $660.15). The within-Nov refunds ($1,087.36) hit BOTH bases equally and cannot produce a gap, which is itself corroboration.
shopify_refund_basis_PROVEN.residual: $86.85 (11.6% of $747.00) — EXPLAINED IN KIND, NOT PROVEN TO THE CENT: `totalRefundedSet` is the GROSS refund including shipping and tax, while Shopify's Net sales excludes both. The shipping/tax component of those refunds is the expected size of this residual. Proving it exactly needs a refund line-item breakdown = one more op, not spent.
shopify_refund_basis_PROVEN.consequence: C11/E5 0.5% tolerance is now PROVEN, not merely hypothesis-consistent.
